lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Toronto Maple Leafs are shedding the ghosts of a 78-point, eighth-in-Atlantic finish to signal a bold new identity, and the most shocking move yet is the hiring of former Ottawa rival Daniel Alfredsson as associate coach. This Hall of Famer, who spent three seasons as an Ottawa assistant, will now command the Leafs' power play under Jim Hiller, a decision that bridges the bitter Battles of Ontario with fresh leadership. The front office also added John Gruden and Brad Werenka while cutting ties with Mike Van Ryn and Derek Lalonde, signaling a complete philosophical reset. With the season firmly in the rearview, the team's focus now shifts to reshaping the roster for next year. What to watch for is how Alfredsson's power-play expertise and the new staff's chemistry translate into a deeper, more aggressive Leafs squad by October.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: After a four-game offensive collapse that saw the Blue Jays score just one point across two losses, Toronto finally ripped the lid off their slumber with a revitalizing 9-3 victory over the Giants, breaking their offensive drought and snapping a dismal losing streak. The Jays, sitting at 43-49 and third in the AL East, are now one game into a win streak after being 11.5 games behind the division leader. The offense, which had been dead in the water against the Mariners and Giants, exploded for nine runs, with Davis Schneider and the rest of the lineup finding their rhythm again. While the team still trails by 3.0 points in the standings, this performance signals a potential turning point. The team heads back to San Francisco today at 3:45 PM ET for a midday showdown, where another strong outing could push them closer to the playoff hunt.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Toronto Raptors' offseason isn't just about reshuffling the roster; it's about honoring a legacy that defined a city. After two decades and one day, Kyle Lowry has officially retired as a Toronto Raptor, signing a ceremonial one-day contract to close his career with the franchise that gave him his greatest moments. The six-time All-Star, who led the Raptors to their lone 2019 NBA championship, will have his No. 7 retired during the 2026-27 season - a tribute to a player many consider the greatest in the team's history. Though the squad finished last year at 46-36, third in the Atlantic Division, that record now serves as a backdrop for what comes next: a new era built on draft picks, free agent moves, and the quiet power of Lowry's departure. What to watch for in the coming weeks is how the front office leverages this emotional transition into a sharper, more competitive roster.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: Washington's secondary isn't just a question mark this summer - it's the entire story, with one cornerback not named Trey Amos expected to dominate snaps in '26 as the unit scrambles to prove it can contain Dallas's aerial assault. Which Commanders CB not named Trey Amos gets the most snaps in '26 looms as camp's defining battle, especially after Trey Amos returned from a fractured fibula and Mike Sainristil posted six interceptions in his first two seasons. The Commanders sit 3rd in the NFC East, trailing by six games, but that 2025 stumble (7-9-1) now frames a fresh mandate: depth chart clarity before preseason. Von Miller's blunt admission - "I picked the wrong team" in 2025 - adds urgency to every edge rusher's camp reps, while seven players aim to rewrite their Washington narratives. Who locks in the slot corner and who starts opposite Sainristil will define whether the Commanders can finally outrun their defensive doubts when they open the season in Philadelphia.

article.title: Wednesday's Skate
paragraphs: The Maple Leafs are signaling a fresh approach by hiring Daniel Alfredsson as an assistant coach, joining John Gruden and Brad Warrena on the staff. Meanwhile, the Blue Jays beat the Giants 9-3 last night and face them again today at 3:45 PM ET on Sportsnet, holding a 43-49 record in third place of the AL East. Over in the NBA, the Raptors are looking forward with Kyle Lowry's retirement announcement and Kawhi Leonard arriving in Toronto for "Kyle Lowry Day." The Washington Commanders are preparing for training camp, with their first game against the Eagles set for Sunday, September 13, in 67 days.

All four Toronto and Washington teams are moving forward with concrete steps: Alfredsson's addition strengthens the Leafs' coaching, the Jays continue their revitalizing offensive run, the Raptors welcome new leadership, and the Commanders focus on camp readiness ahead of their September opener.
